description: MECHANISM (mirror of `core-language/check/repcount-in-place-index-key`): a `repcount` inside a well-formed place's `[ … ]` index key is a REAL read that the evaluator really evaluates, so it must be judged like any other read (issue #1155). The proof is the printed value: `:xs` starts `[ 1 2 ]` and ends `[ 5 5 ]`, which only happens if turn 1 resolved the key to index 1 and turn 2 to index 2 — the enclosing `repeat`'s turn, read from inside an assignment TARGET. Silence alone would not show that; the list contents do. This is why the rule skips only a target that is not a well-formed place (where `ol-not-a-place` already describes the whole fault) instead of skipping every assignment target, which would blind it to this read.
